proposals.before: In the eighth month he drove the rebels to Altishahr and then to Lake Yashilkul, where the Muslim communities submitted.
proposals.after: In the eighth month he drove the rebels to Alchur and then to Lake Yashilkul, where the Muslim communities submitted.
proposals.reason: 阿勒楚爾 is Alchur in this pursuit narrative, not Altishahr (a broader Tarim oasis label).

proposals.before: In the eighth month he pursued the rebels to Altishahr and then to Lake Yashilkul; the Muslim populace submitted.
proposals.after: In the eighth month he pursued the rebels to Alchur and then to Lake Yashilkul; the Muslim populace submitted.
proposals.reason: Same place-name error as in the idiomatic rendering: 阿勒楚爾 should not be translated as Altishahr.

proposals.before: He proposed garrison colonies at Manas, Kur, Karasu, and Jinghe, with fifteen mu allotted to each settler.
proposals.after: He proposed garrison colonies at Manas-Kur, Karasu, and Jinghe, with fifteen mu allotted to each settler.
proposals.reason: Chinese names three places (三地): 瑪納斯庫爾、喀喇烏蘇、晶河; English incorrectly splits into four.

proposals.before: He memorialized on garrison farming at Manas, Kur, Karasu, and Jinghe, allotting fifteen mu per person.
proposals.after: He memorialized on garrison farming at Manas-Kur, Karasu, and Jinghe, allotting fifteen mu per person.
proposals.reason: Same three-place count mismatch: 三地 must remain three locations, not four.

proposals.before: The emperor blamed them for the delay, saying it had shown weakness and cost imperial prestige; although the ministry recommended dismissal, he kept them in office and stationed A Gui at Yarkand.
proposals.after: The emperor blamed them for the delay, saying it had shown weakness and cost imperial prestige; although the ministry recommended dismissal, he kept them in office and stationed A Gui at Yar.
proposals.reason: 雅爾城 is Yar (Tarbagatai), not Yarkand (葉爾羌).

proposals.before: The emperor rebuked them for delay, saying it showed cowardice and damaged prestige; the ministry proposed stripping them of office, but the emperor ordered them to remain in post and garrison Yarkand.
proposals.after: The emperor rebuked them for delay, saying it showed cowardice and damaged prestige; the ministry proposed stripping them of office, but the emperor ordered them to remain in post and garrison Yar.
proposals.reason: 雅爾城 is Yar, not Yarkand.

proposals.before: A Gui proposed relocating the Yarkand garrison to Chuchu, and the court approved.
proposals.after: A Gui proposed relocating the Yar garrison city to Chuchu, and the court approved.
proposals.reason: 雅爾城 is Yar, not Yarkand.

proposals.before: A Gui memorialized to move Yarkand to Chuchu, and the request was granted.
proposals.after: A Gui memorialized to move Yar city to Chuchu, and the request was granted.
proposals.reason: 雅爾 is Yar, not Yarkand.

proposals.before: He asked that three courier stations be established from Chuchu to Urtubulak to open communications with Yarkand, and the ministries were ordered to carry this out.
proposals.after: He asked that three courier stations be established from Chuchu to Urtubulak to open communications with Yar, and the ministries were ordered to carry this out.
proposals.reason: 雅爾 is Yar, not Yarkand.

proposals.before: He requested that three courier stations be set up from Chuchu to Urtubulak to link with Yarkand; the matter was referred to the relevant ministry for implementation.
proposals.after: He requested that three courier stations be set up from Chuchu to Urtubulak to link with Yar; the matter was referred to the relevant ministry for implementation.
proposals.reason: 雅爾 is Yar, not Yarkand.

proposals.before: By then the Jinchuan chieftain Langka was dead, but his son Sonom and Zewang's son Senggesang of Lesser Jinchuan were raiding the frontier; Governor-General Ertai's campaign had failed, and the emperor ordered A Gui to join Deputy Commander Wenfu in the advance.
proposals.after: By then the Jinchuan chieftain Langka was dead, but his son Sonom and Zewang's son Senggesang of Lesser Jinchuan were raiding the frontier; Governor-General Altai's campaign had failed, and the emperor ordered A Gui to join Deputy Commander Wenfu in the advance.
proposals.reason: 阿爾泰 is Altai/A'ertai; Ertai risks confusion with Ortai (鄂爾泰).

proposals.before: At that time the Jinchuan chieftain Langka was already dead; his son Sonom and the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang's son Senggesang were harassing the border; Sichuan governor-general Ertai campaigned against them without success, and the emperor ordered A Gui to follow Deputy Commander and Minister Wenfu in the advance.
proposals.after: At that time the Jinchuan chieftain Langka was already dead; his son Sonom and the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang's son Senggesang were harassing the border; Sichuan governor-general Altai campaigned against them without success, and the emperor ordered A Gui to follow Deputy Commander and Minister Wenfu in the advance.
proposals.reason: 阿爾泰 should be Altai/A'ertai, not Ertai.

proposals.before: Vice Minister Guilin had replaced Ertai as governor-general and led his troops to Molong Ravine, where they were beaten and Vice Commander Xue Cong was killed; Ertai impeached Guilin and had him removed.
proposals.after: Vice Minister Guilin had replaced Altai as governor-general and led his troops to Molong Ravine, where they were beaten and Vice Commander Xue Cong was killed; Altai impeached Guilin and had him removed.
proposals.reason: Consistent correction of Ertai to Altai for 阿爾泰.

proposals.before: At that time Vice Minister Guilin replaced Ertai as governor-general and also took over his forces; reaching Molong Ravine, he met defeat and Vice Commander Xue Cong was killed; Ertai impeached and had Guilin dismissed.
proposals.after: At that time Vice Minister Guilin replaced Altai as governor-general and also took over his forces; reaching Molong Ravine, he met defeat and Vice Commander Xue Cong was killed; Altai impeached and had Guilin dismissed.
proposals.reason: Consistent correction of Ertai to Altai for 阿爾泰.

proposals.before: Following the tribal guide Mutar, they split the force along central and southern routes while secretly posting men on the northern ridge, then seized Meinuo. Mingliang's column also took Sengge Stockade and linked up. Within seven days, Lesser Jinchuan was subdued.
proposals.after: Using the tribal native Mutar's stratagem, they split the force along central and southern routes while secretly posting men on the northern ridge, then seized Meinuo. Mingliang's column also took Sengge Stockade and linked up. Within seven days, Lesser Jinchuan was subdued.
proposals.reason: Chinese 用番人木塔爾策 means employing Mutar's plan/stratagem (策), not that Mutar served as a guide.

proposals.before: Meanwhile Fengsheng'e was moving along the northern route; when his column reached Kailiye and saw the beacon fires, he knew the main army was coming to link up.
proposals.after: Meanwhile Fengsheng'e was moving along the northern route; when his column reached Kailiye and saw the beacon fires, he brought his army to join them.
proposals.reason: Chinese 以師來會 means he came with his troops to rendezvous, not that he inferred the main army was coming to him.

proposals.before: At this time Fengsheng'e was advancing from the northern route; when his army reached Kailiye and saw signal fires, he knew the main force had come to join him.
proposals.after: At this time Fengsheng'e was advancing from the northern route; when his army reached Kailiye and saw signal fires, he came with his army to join them.
proposals.reason: Literal English reverses 以師來會; Fengsheng'e is the one who advances to join.

proposals.before: In the forty-second year the acting Yunnan-Guizhou governor Tusi De memorialized: "Meng Bo is dead; his son Zhuajiaoya has succeeded, professes loyalty, offers tribute, and wishes to return to Chinese rule.
proposals.after: In the forty-second year the acting Yunnan-Guizhou governor Tuside memorialized: "Meng Bo is dead; his son Zhuajiaoya has succeeded, professes loyalty, offers tribute, and is willing to return Chinese subjects.
proposals.reason: 圖思德 is one Manchu name (Tuside), not 'Tusi De'; 原/願歸中國人 means returning Chinese people/captives, not returning to Chinese rule.

proposals.before: Zhejiang financial commissioner Sheng Zhu reported that Governor Chen Huizu was privately tied to the family of Wang Tanwang; the emperor ordered A Gui to Zhejiang to investigate.
proposals.after: Zhejiang financial commissioner Sheng Zhu reported that Governor Chen Huizu had privately appropriated property while confiscating the household of Wang Tanwang; the emperor ordered A Gui to Zhejiang to investigate.
proposals.reason: 籍…家有所私 means private appropriation during confiscation of Wang Tanwang's household, not a personal tie to that family.

proposals.before: Zhejiang financial commissioner Sheng Zhu memorialized that Governor Chen Huizu had private ties to the family of Wang Tanwang; the emperor ordered A Gui to go to Zhejiang to investigate.
proposals.after: Zhejiang financial commissioner Sheng Zhu memorialized that Governor Chen Huizu had privately appropriated something while confiscating Wang Tanwang's household; the emperor ordered A Gui to go to Zhejiang to investigate.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 籍王亶望家有所私 is confiscation-related embezzlement, not private family ties.

proposals.before: At dusk his generals urged him: "We must seize Sonom tonight, or he may yet slip away."
proposals.after: At dusk his generals urged him: "We must take Sonom alive today, or something else may happen."
proposals.reason: Chinese 今日必生致索諾木 means take Sonom alive today, not seize him tonight; 慮有他 is fear of some other outcome.

proposals.before: A Gui had his escort dismount, hung their cloaks on the trees to resemble additional troops, remounted, and rode slowly down the slope.
proposals.after: A Gui ordered his escort to dismount, strip off their clothes and hang them on the trees, then remount and descend the mound slowly.
proposals.reason: Chinese 解衣裂懸林木 is stripping/tearing clothes to hang on trees; 'cloaks' and the purpose clause are not in this sentence.
